newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: BT and NS see one bln dfl Dutch investment.
newsitem.headline: BT and NS see one bln dfl Dutch investment.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc (BT) and Dutch state-owned rail firm Nederlandse Spoorwegen (NS) said on Wednesday they would invest one billion guilders over the coming four or five years in a Dutch telecom infrastructure should they win a new licence.

BT and NS said last week they had submitted an application for one of a possible two licences to build and operate a national fixed-line public telephone network in the Netherlands in competition with current fixed-line monopolist Koninklijke PTT Nederland (Dutch PTT).

The new venture, to be called "Telfort", will involve investment from the two partners on a 50:50 basis. Announcing the name, new managing director Koos van der Meulen said: "We're speaking of investing around one billion guilders in the coming years," adding that would be over four or five years.
He saw turnover in the first year at around 150 million guilders, rising by a factor of 10 to between 1.5 billion and two billion guilders after 10 years.
The current staff level of around 250 people was on track to rise to 1,000-1,500 in the coming years, said Van der Meulen, formerly managing director of BT Nederland.

BT Nederland has been represented in the Netherlands since 1989 and currently offers business communications to Dutch-based multinationals via its "Concert" joint venture with MCI, the second largest carrier in the United States.
Key customers for Concert in the Netherlands include Shell, Philips, ABN AMRO, Unilever and Reed Elsevier.

Pat Gallagher, director of BT Europe told the news conference: "We are delighted to have reached this stage in the development of our plans for the Dutch market. In NS we have found a partner which shares our vision for extending telecommunications choice in the Netherlands."

Telfort will initially offer data, corporate voice and virtual private networks, as well as international voice and data services from Concert. The new venture will also offer management and outsourcing with a full national portfolio of products and services once a licence has been awarded.
The Dutch transport ministry, which oversees telecoms, has said it could award one or two licences and expects to announce its decision before the end of this year.
The Netherlands plans full liberalisation of its telecoms market, the fifth largest in Europe valued at around 15 billion guilders, by January 1, 1998.

Telfort said it was developing plans to serve the Dutch residential market and mobile market. "Our mission is that we're the alternative for national and international telephony services. The alternative in the Netherlands," said Van der Meulen.

Gallagher said he was confident that Telfort would win a new Dutch licence. "We've already got a vast range of business operations, we're here already...to be told that we're not the prime candidate is unthinkable," he told reporters after the news conference.

Two other groups have submitted applications for Dutch fixed line licences. One is Enertel, a consortium of Dutch regional power companies and local cable television network operators. The other is Global One, a joint venture of Sprint Corp, France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
